label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/insecure-randomness): alert-TP — java.util.Random().nextGaussian() at L67 produces a pseudo-random value that flows through Double.toString() and substring() to become rememberMeKey at L68. This rememberMeKey is then used as the value for a remember-me cookie (L96-97) and stored in the session (L101). Using java.util.Random (cryptographically insecure PRNG) to generate authentication/session tokens is a real vulnerability; SecureRandom should be used instead. Alert 2 (java/xss): alert-FP — resolved sink value at L105-110 is a concatenation of: (1) user = "Gayle" + className-derived suffix (both hardcoded/server-controlled), (2) rememberMe.getName() = "rememberMe" + className-derived suffix (server-controlled), (3) rememberMe.getValue() = rememberMeKey (derived from java.util.Random, not user input). All three components are server-generated constants or application-controlled values; none depend on user-provided input. Case TP driven by Alert 1.
